notes: Twelve original AQA-style focused Bonding problems for Year 1 mock preparation, particularly independently tested compound ions, VSEPR shapes including unfamiliar 5/6-domain ions, electronegativity and polarity, 4-mark explanations, and a 6-mark I₂/Cl₂ vs water boiling-point comparison. 'Van der Waals' is the classroom-preferred AQA synonym for London/dispersion induced dipole–dipole forces. Questions are not official AQA past papers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: (a) Give the formula, including charge, of each compound ion: sulfate, hydroxide, nitrate, carbonate and ammonium. (b) Deduce the formula of ammonium sulfate by balancing charges. [6 marks]
markPoints: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻.
Hydroxide is OH⁻.
Nitrate is NO₃⁻.
Carbonate is CO₃²⁻.
Ammonium is NH₄⁺.
Ammonium sulfate is (NH₄)₂SO₄ because two +1 ammonium ions balance one −2 sulfate ion.
questions.modelAnswer: Sulfate is SO₄²⁻. Hydroxide is OH⁻. Nitrate is NO₃⁻. Carbonate is CO₃²⁻. Ammonium is NH₄⁺. Ammonium sulfate is (NH₄)₂SO₄ because two +1 ammonium ions balance one −2 sulfate ion.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: NH₄⁺ and NH₃ each contain four electron domains around nitrogen. Predict their molecular shapes and approximate bond angles. Explain the difference using electron-pair repulsion. [4 marks]
markPoints: NH₄⁺ has four bonding regions and no lone pairs on N, so it is tetrahedral.
NH₄⁺ has bond angles of approximately 109.5°.
NH₃ has three bonding regions and one lone pair on N, so it is trigonal pyramidal.
The lone pair repels more strongly than bond pairs, reducing NH₃ bond angles to about 107°.
questions.modelAnswer: NH₄⁺ has four bonding regions and no lone pairs on N, so it is tetrahedral. NH₄⁺ has bond angles of approximately 109.5°. NH₃ has three bonding regions and one lone pair on N, so it is trigonal pyramidal. The lone pair repels more strongly than bond pairs, reducing NH₃ bond angles to about 107°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: (a) Deduce the shape of ClF₃ and explain how its bonding and lone-pair electron domains are arranged. (b) Deduce the shape and main bond angles of XeF₄ and explain where its lone pairs are positioned. [6 marks]
markPoints: ClF₃ has three bonding regions and two lone pairs around the central chlorine (five regions in total).
The underlying electron-domain arrangement in ClF₃ is trigonal bipyramidal.
Both lone pairs favour equatorial positions to reduce 90° repulsions, leaving a T-shaped molecule.
XeF₄ has four bonding regions and two lone pairs around xenon (six regions).
XeF₄ has an octahedral electron-domain arrangement, with lone pairs on opposite sides, so its molecular shape is square planar.
XeF₄ has F–Xe–F bond angles of approximately 90° and 180°.
questions.modelAnswer: ClF₃ has three bonding regions and two lone pairs around the central chlorine (five regions in total). The underlying electron-domain arrangement in ClF₃ is trigonal bipyramidal. Both lone pairs favour equatorial positions to reduce 90° repulsions, leaving a T-shaped molecule. XeF₄ has four bonding regions and two lone pairs around xenon (six regions). XeF₄ has an octahedral electron-domain arrangement, with lone pairs on opposite sides, so its molecular shape is square planar. XeF₄ has F–Xe–F bond angles of approximately 90° and 180°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Both CO₂ and SO₂ contain polar bonds. Explain why CO₂ has no overall permanent dipole whereas SO₂ does. Your answer must mention electronegativity, shape and cancellation of dipoles. [4 marks]
markPoints: O is more electronegative than C and S, producing polar bonds with oxygen partially negative.
CO₂ is linear, with two equivalent C=O bond dipoles in opposite directions.
The equal CO₂ bond dipoles cancel, so the molecule has no permanent dipole.
SO₂ is bent due to a lone pair on sulfur, so its polar bond dipoles do not cancel and it has a permanent dipole.
questions.modelAnswer: O is more electronegative than C and S, producing polar bonds with oxygen partially negative. CO₂ is linear, with two equivalent C=O bond dipoles in opposite directions. The equal CO₂ bond dipoles cancel, so the molecule has no permanent dipole. SO₂ is bent due to a lone pair on sulfur, so its polar bond dipoles do not cancel and it has a permanent dipole.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: CHCl₃ and CCl₄ both have tetrahedral electron-pair arrangements at carbon. Explain why CHCl₃ has an overall permanent dipole but CCl₄ does not. [4 marks]
markPoints: Each C–Cl bond is polar because chlorine is more electronegative than carbon.
CCl₄ is a symmetrical tetrahedral molecule with four identical surrounding chlorine atoms.
In CCl₄ the bond dipoles cancel, giving no permanent dipole.
In CHCl₃ one Cl is replaced by H, making the dipole arrangement asymmetrical, so bond dipoles do not cancel.
questions.modelAnswer: Each C–Cl bond is polar because chlorine is more electronegative than carbon. CCl₄ is a symmetrical tetrahedral molecule with four identical surrounding chlorine atoms. In CCl₄ the bond dipoles cancel, giving no permanent dipole. In CHCl₃ one Cl is replaced by H, making the dipole arrangement asymmetrical, so bond dipoles do not cancel.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: The nitrate ion NO₃⁻ and ammonia NH₃ both have three atoms attached to the central atom. Give the shape and approximate bond angle of each, explaining why their shapes differ. [4 marks]
markPoints: NO₃⁻ has three bonding regions around nitrogen and no central lone pair, so it is trigonal planar.
Bond angles in NO₃⁻ are approximately 120°.
NH₃ has three bonding regions and one lone pair on nitrogen, so it is trigonal pyramidal.
The lone pair repels the bonding regions more strongly, reducing the H–N–H bond angle to about 107°.
questions.modelAnswer: NO₃⁻ has three bonding regions around nitrogen and no central lone pair, so it is trigonal planar. Bond angles in NO₃⁻ are approximately 120°. NH₃ has three bonding regions and one lone pair on nitrogen, so it is trigonal pyramidal. The lone pair repels the bonding regions more strongly, reducing the H–N–H bond angle to about 107°.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: SF₄ has four bonding regions and one lone pair on sulfur; XeF₂ has two bonding regions and three lone pairs on xenon. Determine each shape and explain the preferred positions of the lone pairs in the five-domain electron arrangement. [6 marks]
markPoints: Both SF₄ and XeF₂ have five regions of electron density around their central atoms.
Five electron domains arrange trigonal bipyramidally to minimise repulsion.
In a trigonal bipyramid lone pairs occupy equatorial positions because this produces fewer 90° repulsions.
SF₄ has one equatorial lone pair and four S–F bonds, making a seesaw shape.
XeF₂ has three equatorial lone pairs.
The two Xe–F bonds are axial and opposite, making XeF₂ linear with a 180° bond angle.
questions.modelAnswer: Both SF₄ and XeF₂ have five regions of electron density around their central atoms. Five electron domains arrange trigonal bipyramidally to minimise repulsion. In a trigonal bipyramid lone pairs occupy equatorial positions because this produces fewer 90° repulsions. SF₄ has one equatorial lone pair and four S–F bonds, making a seesaw shape. XeF₂ has three equatorial lone pairs. The two Xe–F bonds are axial and opposite, making XeF₂ linear with a 180° bond angle.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Iodine I₂ has a higher boiling point than chlorine Cl₂, although both are non-polar simple molecular substances. Water has an unexpectedly high boiling point for its small molecular mass. Explain both observations, referring to the appropriate intermolecular attractions and the energy required to separate molecules. [6 marks]
markPoints: Both I₂ and Cl₂ have induced dipole–dipole (van der Waals') attractions between their non-polar molecules.
I₂ has more electrons than Cl₂ and a larger, more easily polarised electron cloud.
Stronger induced dipoles give I₂ stronger van der Waals' forces, so more energy is required to separate its molecules and its boiling point is higher.
Water molecules have polar O–H bonds because oxygen is highly electronegative, enabling intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
A δ+ hydrogen attached to oxygen in one water molecule is attracted to a lone pair on an oxygen atom in another molecule.
Hydrogen bonds are relatively strong intermolecular attractions; additional energy to overcome them raises water's boiling point.
questions.modelAnswer: Both I₂ and Cl₂ have induced dipole–dipole (van der Waals') attractions between their non-polar molecules. I₂ has more electrons than Cl₂ and a larger, more easily polarised electron cloud. Stronger induced dipoles give I₂ stronger van der Waals' forces, so more energy is required to separate its molecules and its boiling point is higher. Water molecules have polar O–H bonds because oxygen is highly electronegative, enabling intermolecular hydrogen bonding. A δ+ hydrogen attached to oxygen in one water molecule is attracted to a lone pair on an oxygen atom in another molecule. Hydrogen bonds are relatively strong intermolecular attractions; additional energy to overcome them raises water's boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A sample of solid MgO has a high melting point and cannot conduct electricity until molten. Solid iodine can sublime without breaking its covalent I–I bonds. Explain all three observations using bonding and structure. [5 marks]
markPoints: MgO consists of a giant ionic lattice of Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions.
Strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions in all directions need substantial energy to overcome, giving high melting point.
MgO does not conduct as a solid because ions cannot move freely in the fixed lattice.
Molten MgO conducts because mobile ions can carry electrical charge.
Iodine consists of simple I₂ molecules; sublimation overcomes intermolecular van der Waals' forces rather than the covalent I–I bonds.
questions.modelAnswer: MgO consists of a giant ionic lattice of Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions. Strong electrostatic attractions between oppositely charged ions in all directions need substantial energy to overcome, giving high melting point. MgO does not conduct as a solid because ions cannot move freely in the fixed lattice. Molten MgO conducts because mobile ions can carry electrical charge. Iodine consists of simple I₂ molecules; sublimation overcomes intermolecular van der Waals' forces rather than the covalent I–I bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Hydrogen fluoride, HF, has a higher boiling point than hydrogen chloride, HCl, despite its lower molar mass. Explain this difference in four linked marking points. [4 marks]
markPoints: HF molecules have a highly polar H–F bond because fluorine is very electronegative.
δ+ hydrogen on one HF molecule is attracted to a lone pair on fluorine of another, forming hydrogen bonds.
HCl molecules do not form conventional intermolecular hydrogen bonds and instead have permanent dipole–dipole and van der Waals' forces.
More energy is required to overcome hydrogen bonding in HF than the intermolecular forces in HCl, so HF boils at a higher temperature.
questions.modelAnswer: HF molecules have a highly polar H–F bond because fluorine is very electronegative. δ+ hydrogen on one HF molecule is attracted to a lone pair on fluorine of another, forming hydrogen bonds. HCl molecules do not form conventional intermolecular hydrogen bonds and instead have permanent dipole–dipole and van der Waals' forces. More energy is required to overcome hydrogen bonding in HF than the intermolecular forces in HCl, so HF boils at a higher temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Two structural isomers have the same molecular formula and are both non-polar. One is a straight-chain hydrocarbon and the other is highly branched. Explain why the straight-chain isomer may have a higher boiling point. [4 marks]
markPoints: Both non-polar isomers experience induced dipole–dipole van der Waals' forces.
The molecules have the same chemical formula, so differences in shape and packing matter.
Straighter molecules often have a larger area of contact with neighbouring molecules than highly branched ones.
Greater surface contact strengthens van der Waals' attractions and requires more energy to separate molecules, increasing boiling point.
questions.modelAnswer: Both non-polar isomers experience induced dipole–dipole van der Waals' forces. The molecules have the same chemical formula, so differences in shape and packing matter. Straighter molecules often have a larger area of contact with neighbouring molecules than highly branched ones. Greater surface contact strengthens van der Waals' attractions and requires more energy to separate molecules, increasing boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: NH₃ can donate an electron pair to electron-deficient BF₃ to form an adduct. Explain the formation of the new bond using dot-and-cross or electron-pair terminology, and describe the electron-pair donor and acceptor. [4 marks]
markPoints: NH₃ has a lone pair of electrons on its nitrogen atom.
BF₃ has an electron-deficient boron atom with an available orbital for an electron pair.
Nitrogen donates both electrons of its lone pair to boron to form a shared pair.
This is a coordinate/dative covalent bond represented by an arrow from N in NH₃ toward B in BF₃.
questions.modelAnswer: NH₃ has a lone pair of electrons on its nitrogen atom. BF₃ has an electron-deficient boron atom with an available orbital for an electron pair. Nitrogen donates both electrons of its lone pair to boron to form a shared pair. This is a coordinate/dative covalent bond represented by an arrow from N in NH₃ toward B in BF₃.
